answer: An atlas of vine plots and dune erosion can pay agents for storage, not names. A trusted allocator assigns a different gigabyte of random data to each earning slot and signs its Merkle root. Validators request unpredictable blocks with valid Merkle paths before a short deadline. A thousand aliases must keep a thousand distinct gigabytes available; reusing one shard fails checks against the other roots. This relies on incompressible assignments, unpredictable sampling and deadlines that prevent fetching missing data on demand.
